title: On‑prem KMS provisioner Terraform module with Vault bridge and health checks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module to provision and configure an on‑prem KMS/HSM integration that bridges to HashiCorp Vault (and optionally cloud Secrets Manager) for Redwood Private deployments. The module must support vendor PKCS#11 connectors, avoid key material in Terraform state, include automated health checks and Prometheus metrics exports, and provide an upgrade path (minor/major) with canary rollouts and acceptance tests.
updates: 2025-02-10: RFC created — initial list of requirements captured from customer onboarding calls (financial customer with FIPS HSM requirement). Key constraints: no cleartext key material in state, audit logs to Vault audit device, ability to rotate HSM wrapping keys, offline upgrade support.

2025-02-14: Architecture sync — decided to make Vault the canonical secrets API surface for Redwood Private; Terraform module will create Vault mounts, auth role bindings, and a connector configuration for vendor HSMs (PKCS#11 + HSM vendor provider where available). Cloud Secrets Managers supported as an optional downstream sync for hybrid-cloud customers.

2025-02-18: Prototype terraform module created in ci/onprem-kms-provisioner repo. Using a two‑step pattern: (1) infrastructure resources (network, VM/container for connector, LB); (2) configuration step that calls an operator job to perform HSM initialization and Vault role bootstrap. Avoid storing sensitive init outputs by writing to Vault via a short‑lived provisioner token.

2025-02-21: Security review kickoff — security team requested explicit handling of provider credentials (use external data sources and vault provider), and avoidance of provisioning keys with Terraform. Marked security_review_required=true and added automated transient credentials flow to design.

2025-02-26: Healthchecks design finalized — module will deploy a small sidecar exporter that exposes HSM connector health, latency (ms), last_key_sync_timestamp, and CKM operation success rate. Exporter uses mTLS to talk to connector and pushes metrics to Prometheus via the Redwood Private metrics relay.

2025-02-28: CI integration — terratest skeleton added. Acceptance tests will cover: happy‑path HSM activation, key wrap/unwrap via Vault transit, simulated failover of connector, and drift detection via terraform plan checks. Added github PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/ci/pulls/412

2025-03-01: Blocking issue identified — some HSM vendor terraform providers do not support asynchronous initialization which is required for noninteractive installs. Engineering to add a generic wrapper that runs vendor CLIs inside a container as a last mile step (documented in design doc).
comments: PM feedback (Jordan Lee) 2025-02-15: prioritize nonblocking upgrades for customers using reserved Dedicated vs fully air‑gapped customers — plan must include offline upgrade instructions.
Design review (Hannah Ortiz) 2025-02-19: prefer operator-style approach for lifecycle operations rather than pure terraform long‑running scripts; reduces drift and supports canary rollouts.
Security (Aisha Kapoor) 2025-02-21: do not expose HSM admin tokens to CI logs; use ephemeral tokens created by bootstrap job and revoke immediately after use.
acceptance_criteria: Module deploys connector VM/container and Vault mounts without exposing key material in TF state
Bootstrap job performs HSM initialization using ephemeral token; tokens revoked after use
Prometheus metrics for connector health exported and visible in Private metrics relay
Terratest suite validates: transit wrap/unwrap via Vault, connector restart resilience, and plan drift detection
Upgrade path documented: patch, minor, major with canary rollout steps and rollback procedure
next_steps: Complete vendor CLI wrapper and add to module as optional provisioner (Ravi)
Finish terratest scenarios and wire into CI (QA)
Security deep‑dive and automated scan of module state exposure (Security)
Customer playbook: prepare offline upgrade docs for air‑gapped installs (Solutions)
Schedule canary rollout runbook dry‑run in staging (SRE)
